steps.what: Prepare undergraduate-level classes by reviewing objectives and assembling existing course resources
Teach undergraduate-level courses, explain concepts and respond to questions

tasks.design: Use reusable class resource collections in {LMS} and {DOCS} to reduce repeated assembly of existing materials. The assistant checks their fit and retains teaching, explanation and responses to students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing course resources are repeatedly located and assembled for each class.
tasks.enabler_now: Native course collections can preserve links and versions without generating a lesson or replacing teaching.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding questions and adapting an explanation remain situated educational work.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant detects misconceptions through dialogue and changes examples accordingly.
tasks.altitude: Keep live teaching time while spending less preparation time assembling familiar resources.

reach.task: Agree which existing resources and objectives apply to the class
reach.learn: Course scope and methods used in formal teaching

evidence.claim: Native reuse of course resources may reduce assembly time; this is an unmeasured E1 scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing to use existing resources and delivering the class; original material authoring and examination grading are separate tasks and savings must not be added twice.

The assistant selects and verifies course, session objective, resource IDs and versions, access needs and teaching focus in s1; all selection and capture remain within its 12 remaining hours. No machine inference of student needs is assumed.
Use native course collections first; classes already using them gain no new saving. Unique preparation falls back to normal manual work.
The assistant teaches only within locally delegated responsibilities; no new academic decision rights are inferred.
research_questions: Does resource reuse reduce preparation after checking relevance and accessibility?

already_counted.description: Resource selection, checking and session focus

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=12+80=92; gross 8%, less 2 upkeep gives net 6%. Low 0 for existing reuse or sessions requiring wholly new preparation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate student work and record grades

steps.what: Check examination submissions, rubric versions and authorized closed-question answer keys
Grade closed examination items against the checked key and inspect exceptions
Evaluate open assignments and papers and resolve marking exceptions
Reconcile and record grades in the internal marking register

tasks.design: Configure closed-item marking in {LMS} and a checked import to the {OTHER} internal assessment register. The assistant verifies the key, evaluates all open work and reconciles marks; official results and release remain with the authorized examiner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Closed responses are repeatedly matched to a key and checked marks are copied to another register.
tasks.enabler_now: Native assessment tools can mark explicit closed answers and map identifiers without judging open responses.
tasks.still_hard: Rubric interpretation, ambiguous answers and defensible feedback require human marking.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant recognizes valid reasoning not anticipated by a key and escalates contested interpretations.
tasks.altitude: Concentrate marking effort on reasoning and exceptions while keeping examiner accountability.

reach.task: Resolve rubric ambiguities and authorize official results
reach.learn: Delegated marking scope and local examination procedures

evidence.claim: Ans supports closed-question grading and distribution of open questions among markers.
In the Netherlands the examination board appoints examiners who set results; assistant authority must follow the institution's arrangements.
The closed-item workload and record-copying saving are E1 scenarios, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: Boundary is checking submissions, marking and recording a provisional internal register; official result determination, publication and appeals remain unchanged outside it.

The course instructor produces marking instructions and key in the existing assessment process. In s1 the assistant captures and verifies assessment ID, key and rubric versions, item IDs, allowed responses, points, student pseudonymous IDs, submission status and accommodations. Its full 15 hours remain; ambiguous keys go back for clarification without automatic resolution.

s2 includes seven and a half hours for inspection and exception detection; s3 retains 50 hours for open marking and all exceptions. Machine marking applies only to explicit closed items with valid response data; unreadable or nonstandard submissions are manual.

s3 produces the human-reviewed mark list. In s4 the assistant checks student and assessment mappings, totals and duplicate or missing marks in four hours before saving the internal register; unverified rows are held for manual reconciliation.
Use native grading and import first. Existing automatic marking earns no labour saving, and a wholly open assessment would not support this scenario.
unknowns: Closed-item share and existing automated marking
Assistant's exact authority and internal import controls
research_questions: Do trial imports preserve every mark, student identifier and assessment version?
How much marking time remains after key checking and closed-item exceptions?

incremental.description: Maintain key configuration, import mapping and access checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=15+7.5+50+4=76.5; gross 23.5%, less 3 upkeep gives net 20.5%. Low 0 if closed marking and imports already exist or open work dominates. Examiner time is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead discussion, tutorial or laboratory sections

steps.what: Lead discussion sections, tutorials or laboratory sections and respond to student work

tasks.design: Retain live discussion, tutorial support and laboratory supervision, with existing plans in {DOCS} and {LMS}. No new automation is credited inside the section itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Effective facilitation depends on student responses, practical conditions and the direction of discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital resources support the section but do not establish a reduction in live attention.
tasks.still_hard: The assistant must notice misconceptions, unsafe practice and uneven participation.
tasks.human_edge: Responsive questioning and direct observation make the section useful and safe.
tasks.altitude: Live facilitation and supervision duties remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve recurring conceptual problems and laboratory concerns raised in sections
reach.learn: Escalation thresholds and course learning priorities

evidence.claim: Direct discussion and laboratory supervision remain human in this task-specific assessment.

assumptions: Boundary is live section delivery, immediate setup and feedback, not creation of teaching materials or formal grading.
Student responses and observations are gathered directly by the assistant within s1, with all time retained; no structured engagement or competence feed is assumed.
Existing tools remain unchanged and there is no new upkeep, so incremental hours are zero.
research_questions: Is there repeated non-live preparation outside this boundary that should be measured separately?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100; gross and net zero, with no added upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop course teaching materials and answer keys

steps.what: Confirm teaching material requirements and select authoritative course sources
Develop syllabi, visual aids, supplementary notes or answer-key drafts

loop.purpose: Draft course material from the agreed specification and source pack
loop.input: Instructor requirements, objectives, format and selected sources
loop.output: Draft teaching material with claim references and draft solutions where needed
loop.check: Assistant verifies each substantive claim, independently solves proposed answers, checks syllabus facts against the instructor brief and tests whether visuals convey the intended concept
loop.stop: One draft and at most two revisions, then manually write or remove unsupported sections
loop.why_not_simpler: Native templates and resource reuse come first; new explanatory prose and examples require semantic drafting beyond formatting

steps.what: Check teaching materials and answer keys and save a corrected internal version

tasks.design: Reuse {LMS} resources and {DOCS} templates before drafting new explanations with a bounded loop. The assistant checks accuracy and independently validates answer keys, then hands an internal version to the instructor; public course-site release remains in the existing human process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing and adapting explanations, notes and examples takes repeated authoring effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-constrained drafting can provide a first version while course facts and solutions remain checked.
tasks.still_hard: Good prose can conceal incorrect reasoning or inappropriate difficulty.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant connects materials to taught methods and checks the reasoning students must learn.
tasks.altitude: Devote a larger share of authoring time to accuracy, accessibility and course fit.

reach.task: Review course accuracy and authorize student-facing materials

evidence.claim: Easygenerator can draft course content from source documents or presentations.
LessonUp supports rewriting slide text by level or tone and creating word lists.
The proposed authoring saving and answer-key workflow are unmeasured E1 assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is original material authoring through an internal checked draft, not class-specific assembly, teaching, official grading or student-facing publication. Instructor review is unchanged and no saving is credited for it.

The assistant captures format, objectives, source versions, required syllabus facts, notation and accessibility requirements in s1 with all 25 hours retained. No ready pedagogical specification or validated generated answer key is assumed.

s2's 22 remaining hours include briefing, source mapping checks, revisions and fallback; s3's 20 hours retain final independent validation. Faculty-supplied facts are checked against their source, never inferred.
Use native reuse, templates and layout before a model loop; unsupported claims or failed solutions are manually corrected. No student data is necessary for generic resource drafting.
unknowns: Correction effort for actual course subjects
research_questions: Do drafts preserve subject reasoning and independently verified solutions?
Does total authoring time fall after source checks, revisions and instructor corrections?

already_counted.description: Independent validation and corrected internal version

incremental.description: Maintain approved source packs and drafting checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+22+20=67; gross 33%, less 4 upkeep gives net 29%. Low 0 for already reusable resources or failed drafts requiring full rewriting.

role.altitude: Keep teaching, supervision and open marking human while reducing resource assembly, closed-item matching and repeated entry.
reach: Coordinate checked material release with course instructors
role.ambitious_version: An assistant who provides reliable teaching support with less repeated preparation and record copying.
